name: Europe hybrid attacks
value: UK warns Ukraine suppliers of sabotage, 24 Nov
summary: UK security officials warn firms supplying Ukraine of Russian sabotage on 24 Nov; Estonia blames Russia for recent plots
state: On 24 Nov the UK defence ministry and MI5's National Protective Security Authority warned firms supplying Ukraine's military of a higher risk of Russian sabotage, often via proxies using arson (Reuters via Internazionale). Estonia says Russian security services were behind an August arson at a military-vehicle maker and it disrupted an attack on a drone maker; eight Latvian citizens were detained over an arson plot ordered by Russian military intelligence (AP). State-attributed plots keep Watch; no sabotage causing casualties or a major outage was found.
for_you: Firms in defence supply chains can follow the National Protective Security Authority's published guidance on site security and staff awareness. Report suspicious activity near sensitive sites to the police.
rubric_hit: Watch: sabotage attributed to a state — Estonia blames Russian services for arson plots; UK warning of 24 Nov; no casualties or major outage

sources.title: Reuters via Internazionale — UK warns of Russian sabotage threat to companies that supply Ukraine
AP via WRAL — British officials warn UK firms aiding Ukraine to brace for Russian sabotage threats

why: Sabotage, arson and drone incursions over airports and bases are how state confrontation reaches daily life in the UK and Europe.
drivers: Russia–NATO tensions, drone and cyber capabilities, proxy recruitment, elections.

rubric.alert: Repeated airport or infrastructure shutdowns across several countries, or sabotage causing casualties or a major outage.
rubric.watch: Drone incursions close an airport or military base, or a sabotage incident is attributed to a state.
rubric.normal: No significant attributed sabotage or airspace incursions in Europe this week.
